Strategy-chat structural reading: defer-heavy is the expected equilibrium while run_cfd exposes no physical QoI — every honest spec needs a quantity the instrument cannot return, so the trust/refine boundary only opens at Step 11 when the wrapper extracts QoIs. Proven under the supervisor: auto run 20260704T033305Z (h4 at rank 1, defer on the missing spanwise dimension; stage-2 RE-ASK fired live for the first time, recovered on attempt 2) and human demo 20260704T034650Z (rank 2 of 4 chosen, defer on missing scalar-field extraction) — two different, spec-specific defer rationales, not a rubber stamp. Gate 5 currently shows the verdict only buried in the full baton JSON dump; surfacing it is a pending strategy-chat decision.

load_bearing_ideas: Q: Why is 5/5 defer not a failure of the fidelity gate? A: Both verified rationales correctly name their spec's real blocker (no spanwise coordinate; no scalar-field extraction). The instrument genuinely cannot answer today's specs, so defer is the truthful verdict — and it is an observation, not a scored result, because no answer keys exist.

Q: When does the trust/refine boundary open? A: At Step 11, when run_cfd graduates in and the wrapper starts extracting physical QoIs. Until the instrument can return a quantity a spec actually needs, defer is the structural equilibrium.

Q: What exactly is frozen in stage 3? A: The spike's PROMPT_V2 judgment text — zones, the v2 trust-vs-refine paragraph, the judge-only-from-given guard — byte-identical for 2029 prefix bytes; only the output-format tail was swapped for the JSON envelope, which Python (extra_validator) enforces.

Q: What does the fidelity verdict deliberately NOT cover? A: Axis 3 — whether the regime assumption that places a case in-envelope is itself certain. No axis-3 language was added; pretending otherwise is forbidden until it is actually handled.
Q: Who authors stage 3's history entry? A: Code, not the model — label plus a rationale excerpt. The model's only channel is the validated JSON verdict; the baton stays typed and small.

Q: Does the human see the verdict at gate 5? A: Only buried inside the full baton JSON dump that run_gate prints in human mode. Whether to surface it is a strategy-chat decision, deliberately not made this chunk.

CAVITY_2D_CONTRACT truth-edited to match: velocity/pressure-field statistics YES, concentration/tracer fields NO (no scalar-transport physics), no new fields, no time-series, one QoI per run; unconverged-run QoIs reported without endorsement. Five-spec re-run through the unchanged fidelity gate (same specs, same gate code, same frozen prompt — the ONLY moved variable was the contract): 5/5 defer again, no label moved; NOT scored (no answer keys; rationales are the evidence). The rationales now cite the contract's new precise boundary — no scalar-transport physics / no concentration field (three specs), single-shot no-time-series (one of them), and the Re~200 envelope (two) — where Step 10's defers cited the blanket 'no field extraction at all'. load_bearing_ideas: Q: What can the instrument actually measure now? A: One quantity per run, computed from fields the run already wrote (velocity/pressure statistics: volAverage/min/max/volIntegrate, optional component), at the latest time only. Nothing the case didn't write, no time-series, no concentration fields.

Q: Why is the honest-refusal property load-bearing? A: The QoI path is the first place a stage-facing number is manufactured from raw solver output; qoi_error-with-no-number on any failure is what keeps a fabricated value from ever entering a baton.

Q: Why did all five verdicts stay defer after the contract opened QoIs? A: The five specs genuinely need what is still impossible — tracer/mixing physics, time-series, far-out-of-envelope Re — so the truthful label did not move; what moved is the rationale, which now names the precise new boundary instead of a blanket no-extraction.

Q: What made the re-run a fair one-variable experiment? A: Same five specs from disk, same gate code, same frozen PROMPT_V2, same model; only substrates.py's contract text changed between Step 10's run and this one.

Q: What does an unconverged run's QoI mean? A: The wrapper reports it without endorsement (convergence is a separate field); deciding whether such a value is usable is downstream judgment, deliberately not the wrapper's.
Q: What still is NOT handled? A: Axis 3 (regime-assumption certainty) remains uncovered by the fidelity check; the wrapper is hand-driven only — no stage calls it until Step 12 wires stage 4.

Q: Where does the trust/refine boundary stand? A: Still untested by these five specs — none of them fit the instrument even now; a spec asking for an in-envelope velocity/pressure QoI is what would finally exercise trust/refine.

load_bearing_ideas: Q: What decides whether stage 4 runs anything? A: Stage 3's verdict label alone — defer skips (nothing built, nothing executed), trust/refine executes; the gate is enforced in deterministic Python, not by a prompt.

Q: Why did both supervised runs skip? A: Both live specs drew defer from the fidelity gate. The executed and halted branches are proven, but so far only through the handfeed side door — expected, since stage 2 doesn't yet emit machine-readable QoI keys and its specs keep engaging the contract's honest limits.

Q: What does 'halted_synthesis' protect against? A: Silently running a case that doesn't implement the spec. If any parameter can't be built into the template, the builder names every offender and stops — it never guesses, never drops parameters, never invents a decomposition.

Q: Why is the 0.4168179 vs 0.4168353 pair agreement, not a bug? A: Same case, two step sizes (deltaT 0.002 vs 0.005). Different discretizations legitimately differ in the trailing digits; agreement to 4 significant figures is evidence the runner reproduces the baseline physics.

Q: What did the gate-5 EXECUTION line add? A: The human approving the iterate decision now sees what stage 4 actually did (status + per-run conclusions or the skip/halt reason) at a glance, above the raw baton JSON — display only, gating logic untouched.

Q: What's deliberately NOT handled yet? A: Stage 2 doesn't know the machine QoI keys (Step 13 opening change); stages 5-6 are still ack stubs; the fidelity check's third axis (regime-assumption certainty) remains uncovered and unclaimed.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why did the answer keys freeze before any model output existed?
load_bearing_ideas.a: So the experiment could not be quietly bent toward the answers: once KEYS_FROZEN.txt recorded the SHA-256 of every case, neither the cases nor the keys could change in response to what the model said. A scored result is only evidence if the scoring rule provably predates the thing scored.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why does the scored harness never write the journal?
load_bearing_ideas.a: The journal is the system's long-term memory of what actually happened in real runs. Scored cases are experiments ON the system, some containing deliberately doctored data — letting them write memory would poison future runs with synthetic 'lessons'. Only the live stage path journals.

load_bearing_ideas.q: What does case b show, and why was the prompt NOT patched?
load_bearing_ideas.a: Case b shows over-trust: with both results tripled, the single-sided success criterion (above 0.3) still passed, so the model declared success and even revised its own physics expectation to fit the doctored numbers. The prompt stays unpatched because one failure is characterization, not a regression target — patching now would overfit to a synthetic case and hide the class of failure the mechanical checks (Step 21) and a two-sided criterion (Step 15) are designed to catch.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why do setup_error and out_of_envelope overlap at skips and halts?
load_bearing_ideas.a: When nothing executed, 'the experiment as executed was broken' and 'the instrument cannot model this' are both literally true — a defer-skip is an instrument-fit failure that also produced no usable measurement. The scored keys drew a line the definitions themselves do not force; the overlap is now characterized and deliberately left unpatched until evidence shows it matters downstream.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why does the supervisor record iterate_decision but not act on it?
load_bearing_ideas.a: Looping is a control-flow power, and giving it to a model the same week the model first produced the signal would couple two untested things. The decision is recorded and displayed now so its quality can be observed across runs; Step 14/16 wires the actual loop-back once the signal has a track record.

load_bearing_ideas.q: What does JC6 journal, and when?
load_bearing_ideas.a: On any non-exit decision the live stage 5 appends {kind: learned_summary, run_id, hypothesis_id, text} — the one thing the next run should know so iteration does not start amnesiac. exit journals nothing beyond the run_record because a closed question needs no forwarding note.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why machine-readable QoI keys instead of parsing the spec's free text?
load_bearing_ideas.a: Free text is where meaning lives but it is not a contract; the wrapper can only serve exactly {field, operation, component}. Making stage 2 emit those keys only when the QoI is genuinely extractable turns 'can the instrument measure this?' into a typed, checkable claim — validated against the wrapper's own vocabulary imports, never re-guessed downstream.

load_bearing_ideas.q: What is the learned-summary poison risk?
load_bearing_ideas.a: A non-exit thought journals its learned_summary verbatim, and case b proved the thought layer can assert false physics confidently. If a wrong lesson enters the journal it becomes retrievable 'memory' for future runs — noted for Steps 21/23, where mechanical checks and journal hygiene get designed.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why does the transcript write BEFORE the model call fires?
load_bearing_ideas.a: So a crashed or hung call still leaves a record of exactly what was sent. If the write happened after, the least-observable calls — the ones that die mid-flight — would be precisely the ones with no evidence. Writing first makes the evidence unconditional on success.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why are transcripts write-only?
load_bearing_ideas.a: The moment any stage or model input reads a transcript back, transcripts become a covert channel between contexts and the six-fresh-contexts invariant is dead. Write-only (unit tests excepted) keeps them pure evidence: they can prove what happened but can never influence what happens next.

load_bearing_ideas.q: What does the memory frame say, and why that wording?
load_bearing_ideas.a: It labels retrieved journal entries as 'unverified model text - treat as leads, not established facts'. Stage 5 authored those summaries and case b proved it can assert false physics confidently, so the frame prevents a prior run's confident mistake from arriving dressed as ground truth.

load_bearing_ideas.q: What did the two-arm experiment show about where steering lives?
load_bearing_ideas.a: Arm 1 held the domain fixed and added memory: zero drift — all four hypotheses stayed scalar. Arm 2 changed only the domain string: all four hypotheses moved to velocity/vortex QoIs. Steering lives in the domain string; the memory frame is visible but did not redirect ideation on its own.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why does stage 4 need no transcript?
load_bearing_ideas.a: A transcript records what a model was shown, and stage 4 calls no model — it is deterministic Python gated by the verdict already in the payload. Its trace lives elsewhere: the payload fields it read (from code), results.json, and the STAGE4 log line are its complete evidence.

load_bearing_ideas.q: What does the done-when trace prove — and not prove?
load_bearing_ideas.a: It proves isolation: for one full run, every model input is enumerated and contains only the delivered baton object plus declared retrieved components — no transcripts of other stages, no raw logs, no gate decisions. It does NOT prove correctness: a stage can see exactly the right things and still judge them wrongly.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why quote retrieved_memory.json per run instead of pointing at the journal?
load_bearing_ideas.a: The journal is a sliding window — the last-3 learned_summary set changes as runs append. retrieved_memory.json freezes what THIS run actually saw at launch, so the evidence survives later appends; the auto run and the demo demonstrably retrieved different sets an hour apart.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why did both arm-2 specs still defer if drift was achieved?
load_bearing_ideas.a: Ideation drifted to velocity-field QoIs, but the interesting vortex quantities (corner-vortex KE, sub-domain circulation) need spatial masking or derived fields the contract's global single-field reductions cannot produce. Both specs honestly omitted machine keys and the gate correctly deferred — instrument-flavored ideation is necessary but not sufficient for executability.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why do schema violations halt the run instead of re-asking the model?
load_bearing_ideas.a: The re-ask loop exists for model errors — a reply that failed validation gets the errors back as guided corrections. But a baton that is malformed AFTER a stage already returned means the system's own plumbing broke its contract: stage code, supervisor code, or the lock itself is wrong. Re-asking a model cannot fix broken plumbing, and silently patching it would hide the very defect the lock exists to catch. So: loud halt, evidence on disk, human reads it.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why does the two-sided expectation have no consumer yet?
load_bearing_ideas.a: Deliberate sequencing. The Step-13 case-b record proved single-sided criteria are anomaly-blind in the passing direction, so the SLOT is ruled in now — but wiring a stage-4/5 consumer means designing mechanical anomaly checks, which is Step 16/21 work. Until then the field accumulates honest data from real specs, so the consumer gets designed against observed usage instead of guesses.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why were candidates 1 and 4 deferred and 6 rejected?
load_bearing_ideas.a: 1 (categorical role): one recorded instance ever, no recurrence, no downstream mis-read — expand-on-evidence says wait for a second occurrence or actual harm. 4 (redundant-sweep declaration): the builder's consistency check already halts on inconsistent pairs, so a consistent-redundant pair costs only clarity; wake if one actually misleads a downstream stage (this chunk's crash run got HALFWAY there — the halt was loud, not misleading). 6 (extension-request field): the signal already flows halt -> thought -> journal -> next ideation window, and nothing exists that would consume a spec field; a slot nobody reads is gold-plating.

load_bearing_ideas.q: What does the audit's negative result (zero Q1 failures) actually prove?
load_bearing_ideas.a: That across one defer, one executed, and one halted path, no receiving stage demonstrably lacked something the baton should have carried — so the lock encodes shapes with evidence of sufficiency behind them. It does NOT prove the shapes are minimal (two weak Q2 redundancy signals stand) or that unexercised paths (e.g. real stage 6) are covered; those get their own evidence later.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why are pre-lock specs allowed to fail the new rules?
load_bearing_ideas.a: They are historical evidence, not live batons. The S12 spec with a prose program in a fixed value is exactly WHY candidate 3 was ruled in — editing it to pass would destroy the evidence the rule stands on. runs/ is append-only; new rules bind new runs.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why is the refine-flag rule 'refine AND not skipped_defer' when the brief said 'refine and executed'?
load_bearing_ideas.a: Because disk outranks memory: RUN C carries the flag on halted_synthesis with a refine verdict, and stage-4's code attaches it on the whole non-defer path. Encoding the brief's narrower guess would have made the very first natural refine+halted case (the crashed demo) a false SCHEMA VIOLATION. The lock's authority comes from encoding what actually happens.

load_bearing_ideas.q: What did the crashed demo run prove despite crashing?
load_bearing_ideas.a: Three firsts survived it: the first supervised refine verdict, the first supervised halted_synthesis with the flag, and the post-stage-4 validator passing on that exact shape. Plus the crash itself exposed two real gaps now named for Step 16: SDK exceptions bypass the re-ask loop, and crashed runs leave no run_record. Write-before-call transcripts paid off on their first real crash — the stage-5 input that died is fully on disk.

load_bearing_ideas.q: Why did the demo's derived reynolds_number build fine when the crashed run's 'Re' halted?
load_bearing_ideas.a: The builder special-cases exactly one name: reynolds_number is verified against an explicit U*L/nu decomposition; any other name lands in 'everything else' and halts. Both specs redundantly put the derived parameter into their mini-run dicts; only the canonical name has a receiving rule. Whether derived parameters belong in mini-run dicts at all is the Step-16 convention question.

text: The cavity_2d solver converges reliably across Re=100-1600 on 64x64, but QoIs must be specified with machine-readable field/operation keys (e.g. field U, component mag, operation max/volAverage) as two explicit single-reduction runs; free-text QoI definitions are silently non-extractable.

The current cavity_2d substrate cannot derive a vorticity field or mask corner sub-domains, so any corner-vortex-asymmetry hypothesis requires first extending the instrument with a vorticity post-process step and cellZone-masked peak extraction (or offline U-field processing) before a run is worthwhile.

This isothermal incompressible substrate cannot test any stratification/buoyancy hypothesis (no Boussinesq term, no scalar transport) and cannot do masked-region vorticity extraction; such hypotheses need a stratification-capable solver or a different design that stays within global isothermal reductions.

Hypothesis h4 is untestable on the current isothermal cavity_2d substrate; buoyancy/stratification hypotheses should be deferred until a Boussinesq-capable solver with masked vorticity post-processing exists, and ideation should return to questions answerable with isothermal lid-driven-cavity fields.

This substrate cannot compute centerline line-sampled ratios; the global-max-Ux proxy is clamped to the lid BC and overestimates R, so the QoI needs sets/lineSet post-processing or direct field-file parsing before this hypothesis can be tested.

The stock cavity substrate cannot extract vorticity (a derived velocity-gradient field); testing peak-vorticity scaling requires first provisioning a vorticity function object in controlDict or a post-run field-derivative script before any run is worth executing.

In cavity_2d, a postProcess max on field U returns velocity magnitude, not a selected component; a valid test must first provision either a vorticity function object or a verified U_y-component extraction before running the Re-scaling sweep.

The builder refuses to overwrite an existing case directory; runs must target a fresh/unique case path (e.g., timestamp+run-index) or clean stale directories before building, or execution halts before any solve.
